case.presentation: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease who underwent a deceased-donor kidney transplant a few years ago has a remote history of an unprovoked, isolated subsegmental pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe, now 3.5 years ago. She completed roughly three months of apixaban at that time, without hematology follow-up or additional surveillance, and has remained off anticoagulation with no new clotting events. Her routine labs, including serial complete blood counts, metabolic panels, and a recent ferritin of 1059 ng/mL, are stable. She has no ongoing signs or family history of venous thromboembolism or active malignancy on age-appropriate screening. Should the patient resume indefinite anticoagulation given the unprovoked pulmonary embolism?
case.recommendations: Given the remote nature of the prior PE, the absence of recurrence over several years off therapy, and the general lack of consensus on indefinite anticoagulation for all unprovoked PEs (especially more minor ones), we do not recommend restarting anticoagulation at this time. However, given her transplant status and unprovoked PE history, we would order an antiphospholipid antibody panel and bilateral lower extremity venous Doppler ultrasound to inform risk stratification before finalizing the long-term anticoagulation plan. She should be considered at higher risk for recurrence and receive pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis during any future hospitalizations, should avoid prolonged immobility during travel, and should seek immediate medical attention if she develops symptoms suggestive of recurrent VTE (new leg swelling, shortness of breath, or chest pain), with a low threshold for diagnostic imaging. Routine thrombophilia screening beyond antiphospholipid testing is not indicated.
